en: Arthur, thanks for joining us inside.
The rain came at a bad time there,
but you had time to finish the match
and what a match.
Give us an idea of the focus
that you brought to court today.
Yeah, I was very happy
with the performance, you know.
We start, I mean,
I start pretty slow, I was a bit tight,
but I think from 4-3 in the first set
when I won those tough and long rallies,
then just the momentum got my way
and I felt way better, especially on the serve,
because the first couple
of games I didn't serve good at all
and then after was very good, so yeah,
very happy with the performance.
Tight at the start, you say?
The significance of the match, of course,
and then the delay at the beginning?
Yeah, you know, it's not easy.
Like, I came out on the court, of course,
it's a semi-final, you're a bit more nervous,
but then after the rain arrived,
then you got away,
then after you come back and the ball,
I mean, the conditions
are completely different and everything
and all together was a bit tough
to deal with, but I'm pretty happy
with the way I manage.
You're up to six in the race,
I think now, and you've got
this big final ahead tomorrow, of course.
How big a step is this in your career?
I need to focus still on the tournament,
you know, of course, six in the race is cool,
I have a final to play tomorrow,
I'm gonna try to bring the title at home,
to go in New York with a lot of confidence,
and yeah, that's it,
but still focus on the final tomorrow.
Well done. Thank you very much.
